samples.summary: New private `gridRange` reinvents the existing exported helper `rangeOf(grid): Range` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:18), which already computes a grid's bounding box in the same package. The repo expects reuse of the shared coordinate helpers; the only semantic difference is the empty-grid contract (`rangeOf` returns an Infinity range instead of `undefined`), which could have been handled by extending or wrapping `rangeOf` rather than adding a second bounding-box implementation inside the Sheet class. The todo doc even bills this as an "extract and reuse" step, but the extraction landed as a class-private duplicate instead of the existing utility.
samples.evidence: coordinates.ts:18 `export function rangeOf(grid: Grid): Range` vs sheet.ts:2391 `private gridRange(grid: Grid): Range | undefined`

samples.summary: The design-doc wording ("Merged blocks travel with an internal copy") overstates the delivered scope: `copyBuffer` is per-`Sheet` state, so a copy in one worksheet pasted into another falls through to the TSV/HTML branch and loses the merge layout, exactly like the documented external-HTML limitation. The doc records the `rowspan`/`colspan` gap but not the cross-sheet one, so the canonical doc does not describe the actual boundary of the feature.
samples.evidence: copyBuffer is a private field of Sheet (sheet.ts:333) and paste's internal branch requires `this.copyBuffer` (sheet.ts:2209); no workbook-level clipboard exists (grep for copyBuffer shows only sheet.ts).
searchedFor: grep .copy()/.paste( call sites in view layer

samples.summary: Extending the propagate-or-reject rule to *external* (TSV/HTML) pastes is a behavior change beyond carrying our own merge metadata: a large external paste that clips one merged block anywhere in its bounding box is now silently discarded in full, with no feedback (feedback is an explicit non-goal). An alternative that fits the paste path better — drop/unmerge only the clipped block, or reject only the offending cells — was not considered in the doc. Recorded as a scope/approach-fit concern, not a logic bug.
samples.evidence: sheet.ts:2285-2292 computes destRange for all paste kinds and returns early on any partially covered merge

samples.summary: The source-side containment check (`copiedMerges.some((m) => !isRangeInRange(m.range, sourceRange))`) is unreachable through the UI because `copy`/`cut` build their range via `getRangeOrActiveCell`, which already runs `expandRangeToMergedBoundaries` — the branch's own lessons doc admits this. Storing intersecting (rather than contained) merges in the buffer just to reject them later is dead validation; capturing only fully contained blocks, or expanding at copy time, would be simpler.

For an internal paste the destination area is the translated source range regardless of whether the copied grid has any content, so pasting a copied all-blank range over a merged block now deletes that block while writing nothing. That merge-destroying no-content case is not described by the design-doc rule ("the pasted content replaces them") and may not be the intended semantic.
samples.evidence: pasteRange is set unconditionally from sourceRange (sheet.ts:2236) and drives overwrittenMerges deletion (sheet.ts:2287, 2329-2339) even when `grid` is empty

finding.summary: New private `gridRange` reinvents the existing exported helper `rangeOf(grid): Range` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:18), which already computes a grid's bounding box in the same package. The repo expects reuse of the shared coordinate helpers; the only semantic difference is the empty-grid contract (`rangeOf` returns an Infinity range instead of `undefined`), which could have been handled by extending or wrapping `rangeOf` rather than adding a second bounding-box implementation inside the Sheet class. The todo doc even bills this as an "extract and reuse" step, but the extraction landed as a class-private duplicate instead of the existing utility.
finding.evidence: coordinates.ts:18 `export function rangeOf(grid: Grid): Range` vs sheet.ts:2391 `private gridRange(grid: Grid): Range | undefined`

verdict.reason: Verified both cited locations. coordinates.ts:18 defines `export function rangeOf(grid: Grid): Range` computing a grid's bounding box from `parseRef(grid.keys())` min/max; sheet.ts:2391-2409 defines `private gridRange(grid: Grid): Range | undefined` doing the identical computation, differing only by returning undefined for an empty grid (callers at sheet.ts:2265 and sheet.ts:2415). `rangeOf` is exported from the same package and is otherwise unreferenced repo-wide, so this is a genuine second implementation of an existing shared coordinate helper, and the empty-grid contract could have been handled by a one-line wrapper. This falls squarely in the design-fit lens's duplication/reuse lane, which the rubric grades as major. One part of the finding's rationale is inaccurate — docs/tasks/active/20260822-sheet-paste-merge-propagation-todo.md:48-50,58 plans extraction "into `gridRange`", not reuse of `rangeOf` — but that only weakens the narrative, not the substantive duplication. No named refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, no guard makes it unreachable, and downgrading it would rest only on my own severity re-grading.
